The row reads data-answer="no", "Cannot use Studio" in amber, and the detail names what is missing: "Rancher's RBAC does not let this role read an extension, create one or open a terminal in its pod." Count "0 users" matches - there is no cluster-member clusterRoleTemplateBinding on local. Picking Cluster Member in the custom-role picker gives the identical reading, so it is a real computation and not a hardcoded row.
verdicts.defect: There is still no way to grant Studio to Cluster Members from this page, and the disabled checkbox the previous wave found has been removed rather than made to work: the row is now a glyph plus a word plus a "Rules" button into Rancher's own role editor. That is a more honest shape, but the design's promise (tick the box, a cluster member can use Studio) is not offered at all. Making it true means widening the role's rules, and one of the three needs is exec into a pod bound to cluster-admin.

verdicts.evidence: The row reads data-answer="yes", "Can use Studio", detail "Rancher's RBAC lets this role read an extension, create one and open a terminal in its pod". Count "2 users" matches the two cluster-owner clusterRoleTemplateBindings on local (u-mo773yttt4, u-b4qkhsnliz), read with kubectl.
verdicts.defect: No revoke. The row is a reading of Rancher's RBAC with no control on it at all now (the disabled checkbox is gone), so the design's "untick Cluster Owners and Studio stops being reachable for them" cannot be done from here. Studio registers its pages with no permission gate, so revoking is not even expressible in this product.

verdicts.evidence: Every row states a count and every one of them is read from this Rancher rather than drawn: Administrators "1 user", Cluster Owners "2 users", Cluster Members "0 users". Cross-checked with kubectl - one admin globalRoleBinding (user-btc48), two cluster-owner clusterRoleTemplateBindings on local, no cluster-member binding. A count that cannot be read prints as "Rancher would not say" rather than as a zero, and the custom row shows no count at all until a role is chosen.

The fourth row starts at data-answer="unasked", "Not asked", with no count and no Rules button. The picker lists this Rancher's 13 cluster RoleTemplates (Cluster Member, Cluster Owner, Create Projects, Manage Cluster Backups ... View Nodes). Choosing "Manage Nodes" gave "Cannot use Studio", "0 users", a Rules button and the sentence naming the three missing needs; choosing "Cluster Owner" gave "Can use Studio" and "2 users". The choice is written to customRole in ConfigMap barn-studio-settings and was still there after a reload. Reset to "Choose a role..." put the row back to "Not asked" with the count gone and customRole back to "".

The card head reads "Studio can write to this Rancher, so treat access like cluster admin." (data-testid settings-access-intro), and the warning banner under it makes the same point concretely: the third of Studio's three needs is exec into a pod whose ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin.
The last crumb is a <span> (settings-crumb-current) reading "Settings", not an <a>. Clicking it left the URL at /dashboard/barn/settings.

Clicked settings-crumb-extensions: landed on /dashboard/c/local/uiplugins#installed, which is Rancher's own Extensions page - the destination the promise and the cross-cutting note both ask for, rather than the Studio list you are already near.

The catalog row's code-review control renders all three segments with Required selected (aria-checked true) and every button disabled and carrying settings__seg-btn--locked. Same row, outcome column: Required selected, all three buttons disabled and locked. It matches the "Both + extensions team" reading the publish dialog shows for a catalog listing.
The catalog row carries a lock glyph (i.icon-lock in the title), the chip "Org policy", and the muted background rgb(247,248,250) against the plain rows' transparent one. Both its cells are locked.

The second destination row reads "Developer load into this Rancher" with the note "Studio's 'This Rancher' publish: it builds in the pod and points this Rancher at the result. Reversible with 'Remove local install'." It is drawn plain rather than muted, i.e. as part of the ungated iteration half the card's head describes, and its two cells are the only settable ones besides the repository row's outcome.

The first row reads "Your dev preview" with the chip "always", a lock glyph and the muted background rgb(247,248,250); the note is "Hot reload while you work. Nobody else can load it." Both cells are locked at Off.

There is no OCI row. The row that carries the "The gate" chip and the green gate treatment (class settings__dest--gate, background rgb(238,245,239) against the plain rows' transparent) is "Push to a repository", and its own note says why: "Studio pushes to GitHub; it cannot push an OCI artifact, so the design's OCI row is this one."
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: this product has no OCI destination, so the highlighted gate row is a GitHub source push standing in for it. The tag and the highlight are drawn correctly on the row that is actually the gate; there is nothing to fix until an OCI push exists.

verdicts.evidence: Clicked "Notified" on the developer load's code-review control: the segment took the on state and ConfigMap barn-studio-settings went to dev-load.code = "notified" with no Save step. Navigated to /barn/extensions and back and it was still Notified, in the page and in the ConfigMap. Clicked "Off" and both went back. The control is editable and the write is real.

The control is two-way, not three: only Off and Notified render (aria-checked moves between them and the ConfigMap follows), and Required is not offered at all. The row reason says a developer load reaches only this Rancher and is ungated by design, so a third segment would be a setting with no effect.
verdicts.defect: The design's promise cannot be produced: you cannot set Required, so a developer load can never be made to demand an outcome sign-off. This is the deliberate removal recorded in DEPARTURES.md item 5 (the previous build stored Required and the publish dialog admitted it was ignoring it), so the remaining two levels are honest - but the promise as written is still not held.

verdicts.evidence: All three segments render with Off selected and every one disabled and locked. Clicking Notified and Required changed nothing in the page or in the ConfigMap. The row reason says the preview is the pod's own dev server and there is nothing to gate.
Same row, outcome column: Off selected, all three disabled and locked, and clicking does nothing.

Clicked Restart on the nodehealth row (chosen as the least-used pod, since a restart ends any terminal session in it). The row went from "Dev server running · uptime 3h 20m" to "Pod running, not serving yet · uptime 0m" and the pod really was replaced: barn-nodehealth-extension-58f64c4997-xss66 (startTime 2026-08-23T23:05:34Z) became ...-nvwfn (startTime 2026-08-24T02:26:01Z).

One row per extension, each a reading of the pod: "base - Dev server running · uptime 1d 19h", "demo - ... 20h 55m", "nodehealth - ... 3h 20m", with a green dot when the pod is ready, amber while it is starting. The uptimes match the pods (base had restarted 43h earlier, which is the 1d 19h), and after the nodehealth restart the same row correctly read "Pod running, not serving yet · uptime 0m" with an amber dot.

The row and everything behind it work, but the connected state cannot be reached in this environment and I was told not to paste a real credential. Pasting a fake token through the field makes the browser spend it against api.github.com first, GitHub answers 401, connectGithub throws and nothing is stored - the card stayed "Not connected". Seeding Secret barn-settings with a fake gh_token and the barn.rancher.io/gh-token=set annotation reaches the stored path: the card then reads "A token is stored", chip "Rejected by GitHub" (s-chip--warning) and "GitHub rejected the token (Bad credentials)." - GitHub's real answer, asked from an extension pod. The Active pill, the login, the scopes and the authorisation date all need a token GitHub accepts, and no such token exists here. Secret restored to empty.

With a token in Secret barn-settings the card showed the ghost Disconnect button. Clicking it took the card to "Not connected", removed the button, relabelled Reconnect to Connect, and emptied the Secret - kubectl shows barn-settings with no data and no gh-token annotation afterwards. One click, nothing to press after it.

The card head names all the uses ("to import repositories, to push when you publish, and to open the pull request that records the hand-off") but declines the isolation promise instead of repeating it: "Generated extensions are never handed this credential, but the pod they run in can read the Secret it lives in (barn-settings in namespace barn, and that pod is bound to cluster-admin), so treat it as a credential Studio shares with anything it runs."
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's promise that a generated extension never gets this credential is not true in this build, and the card says so rather than making the claim. Making it true means running extension pods under a ServiceAccount that is not cluster-admin, or keeping the token out of a namespace those pods can read.

verdicts.evidence: Clicking Connect/Reconnect reveals a password field (settings-github-token) with the hint "A personal access token with the repo scope is enough" and a link to GitHub with scopes=repo pre-selected. The field is genuinely wired: a pasted token is spent against GitHub on Enter and a bad one is refused rather than stored (the card stayed "Not connected" and the Secret stayed empty). The hint also states plainly that the design's "stored against your user account only" is not true here - there is one Secret for this Rancher's Studio.

The neutral refresh button reads "Connect" with nothing stored and "Reconnect" with a token stored. Clicking it reveals the token field and focuses it (document.activeElement was settings-github-token), which is this product's whole authorisation flow - there is no OAuth round trip to re-run, the credential is a pasted token, and replacing it is what the button opens.

The blue aside at the foot of the sign-off card is titled "Nobody reviews the same extension forty times" and says all three things: changes accumulate against the last published version, there is no per-change approval and nothing to click, the whole run is collapsed into one diff at the push, and "Notified ... never blocks the push".

The last card is headed "What is sent to the model" and states its purpose: "Shown here so you can answer this question without asking the platform team." It then says outright that the rows are what this build does rather than what the design promises.

The third row uses a warning glyph (i.icon-warning, settings__model-icon--warn), not a lock, and splits the design's claim in two: "The design promises two things: redaction on the way out, and a scan again before publish. The scan is real, the redaction is not."
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: nothing redacts anything before the request leaves. The pod's ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin and the GitHub token sits in a Secret that pod can read, so a credential the assistant opens goes to the model as written. Only the second half of the design's promise (the publish-time scan) exists.

verdicts.evidence: The second row also uses the warning glyph rather than a check, and its head reads "The names, shapes and values of cluster resources" - values included. The body: "The design promises kinds, fields and counts with the values redacted. Studio does not redact."
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's promise that values are stripped is not implemented, and the page states the opposite rather than pretending.

There is no Save or Apply button anywhere on the page, and the page says so in its own masthead. Proved the consequence rather than the absence: clicked "Notified" on the developer load's code-review cell, and ConfigMap barn-studio-settings held dev-load.code = "notified" immediately, with no further click. The repository row's code-review control has Required selected and all three segments disabled and locked. Clicking "Off" left policy.repo.code at "required" in the ConfigMap. The row reason says why it is the one fixed cell that is fixed because it is enforced: distributionGate() refuses the distribution until a code sign-off covering the packet is on record.

The repository row's outcome control is the settable three-way one. Drove all three: Notified (start) to Required wrote policy.repo.outcome = "required"; to Off wrote "off" and survived a full page reload drawn as Off; back to Notified wrote "notified". Each click was the write, with no Save step.

The radio is rendered disabled and unchecked. detectPermission() reads the pod's own claude-session.sh and reports --dangerously-skip-permissions, so "Do not ask at all" is the row carrying the "In force" chip. The card's banner says outright that none of the three is settable.
verdicts.defect: Not selectable, so the promised behaviour cannot be produced from this page. It needs --dangerously-skip-permissions dropped from pod/claude-session.sh and a way for the terminal to surface claude's approval prompts. The workspace's own chip can cycle the running session, but claude's cycle has no "ask before every file edit" mode in it, so even that cannot reach this level.

verdicts.evidence: The radio is disabled and unchecked, and it is not the default: "Do not ask at all" is the one marked In force. So neither half of the promise holds.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged on this page. detectPermission() already recognises --permission-mode acceptEdits, so the card would follow the moment pod/claude-session.sh changed. The workspace chip can cycle the running session to "File edits apply, everything else asks" (I drove it), but that is a per-session cycle in the pod, not this card, and a restarted session comes back on the bundle's flag.

verdicts.evidence: The card's banner opens "Not settable, and not per user." and explains that the flag is one line of claude-session.sh in the extension's seed ConfigMap, that Studio rewrites that ConfigMap from the bundle on every page load, and that everybody with a terminal in the pod is at the same level, reached when their session next starts.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: the design's scope claim (per user, in force from the next message) does not hold. It is per pod and it takes effect when a session next starts. The page states the truth instead of the promise.

verdicts.evidence: This is the level in force - the row is checked, carries the success chip "In force" and the warning chip "Admins only, not enforced" - but the radio is disabled, so it is not a choice, and the row itself says the other two halves of the promise are false: "nothing restricts who may open a terminal, and the pod's ServiceAccount is bound to cluster-admin".
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: not selectable, "admins only" is not enforced, and "still cannot publish" is false because the publish path runs from a cluster-admin pod.

verdicts.evidence: The Preview cluster control is a static row reading "local - K3s v1.36.1" with a lock glyph. There is no select, no chevron and no menu inside [data-testid=settings-preview-cluster] (0 select or button elements). The hint says Studio creates every pod in the local cluster, named once in extensions.ts rather than read from a setting.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged: no cluster picker, and nothing for one to write to. The version half of the promise is real and correct (K3s v1.36.1 matches /v3/clusters/local); the choice half does not exist. This Rancher also has only one cluster.

verdicts.evidence: The card head reads "Unpublished extensions only ever load on this cluster. A preview is served by the extension's own pod in namespace barn, reached through this cluster's API proxy, so nothing outside this Rancher can load it." The claim checks out against the preview itself: the editor's iframe src is /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/.

The matrix head has two columns over the destination column: "CODE REVIEW" with an icon-code glyph and "OUTCOME SIGN-OFF" with an icon-eye glyph, and every row draws two independent segmented controls under them. The two are set separately - I moved the repository row's outcome through all three levels while its code cell stayed fixed at Required.

The card head reads "Everything before the push to a repository is iteration, and Studio never interrupts it. The gate is the moment the extension becomes installable by somebody else.", which is the gate the design describes, and the row treatment agrees: the repository row is the one drawn as the gate.
The masthead reads "Studio settings" (h1) over the scope sentence "Applies to everyone who uses Studio on this Rancher." - Rancher-wide, not per project.

The stream ([data-testid=barn-activity-stream]) held 50 entries built from the pod's own record, alternating user prompts and the assistant's replies. Sent "w6-settings-workspace probe 1787537410594" from the composer: a user bubble with that exact text appeared, followed within seconds by an assistant entry, and the stream had scrolled itself to the end (scrollTop 6289 + clientHeight 467 against scrollHeight 6804). It grows as turns arrive and keeps the newest visible.

The composer is a textarea whose placeholder is the worked example the design asks for: 'Describe the next change - e.g. "colour the bars by severity and add a 7-day toggle"'. Typed "line one", Shift+Enter, "line two": the value became "line one\nline two", the placeholder went, and the turn count did not move. Sending it later produced a user turn in the stream.

The clock reads "Snapshot saved Nm ago" and it is a reading of real autosaves: it said 1m ago in one visit and 2m ago in another, and the menu beside it lists the pod's actual snapshot tags ("autosave 0202 on Aug 24 / 2 minutes ago", "autosave 0158 on Aug 24 / 6 minutes ago", ...) which match `git tag` in barn-base-extension (barn-snap/1787537846153 and its neighbours, three minutes apart).

The chip reads "main". `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in barn-base-extension is main, and opening the chip's menu lists the pod's real branches with the current one marked ("barn/base/2", "main current"), which matches `git branch -a` in the pod.

With one file of my own in the pod the banner above the composer read "1 change / Only you can see them. Nothing is asked of you until you publish." and `git status --porcelain` in barn-base-extension listed exactly one entry (verify-w6-settings-workspace.md). After the Undo the count went to zero and the banner disappeared, which is correct - it is drawn only when there is something to review.

The hint under the composer reads "Shift + Enter for a new line · the assistant never publishes on its own", and both halves are true of the control: Shift+Enter mid-sentence inserted a newline and sent nothing (turn count unchanged), while Send/Enter submitted and cleared the draft. With a context path attached the hint extends to "· 1 path named in the message" rather than replacing itself.

The Add chip opened the modal "Add a file to the context" listing the package's real files read from the pod (.gitignore, BRIEF.md, CLAUDE.md, HARNESS.md, babel.config.js, index.ts, l10n/en-us.yaml, package.json, pages/Home.vue, product.ts, routing/index.ts, tsconfig.json). A chip reads "cluster: local" with a server icon. local is the only cluster this Rancher has and the one every extension pod is created in; the masthead's "Preview on: local" and the preview iframe's own path (/k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/...) both agree.

No file chip stands by default, which is honest - nothing is attached.
